metadata.sourceRun: Culinary Integration Results Repair And Contract Acceptance Audit
metadata.runClassification: unversioned documentation-only research, repository audit, and design integration
metadata.scope: documentation-only repair and contract acceptance audit; no implementation permission

acceptedContracts.servingSemantics: authored culinary reference resolving to count, mass, or volume
acceptedContracts.authoritativeAmount: integer or fixed-point canonical basis units

percentageViews.sourceAllocation: allocation across selected servings cannot exceed available physical amount
percentageViews.servingComposition: normalized presentation on an explicitly labeled physical basis

acceptedContracts.nutritionFormula: amount consumed / nutrition basis amount * nutrient value per basis amount; meal total is the sum of ingredient contributions
acceptedContracts.legacyDailyCalories100Posture: observed legacy game-scale body-state rule, not accepted future calorie authority
acceptedContracts.mysteryManifestResolution: merchant stock generation or sale transaction immediately before transfer; never opening
acceptedContracts.assortmentFrameworkScope: reusable market/economy authority with culinary and nonculinary consumers

assortmentStockPostures.clearance: finite opening/rollover stock, normally no same-day replenishment, short withdrawal or expiry window
assortmentStockPostures.freshStandard: finite production-batch stock with authored replenishment intervals
assortmentStockPostures.selectLuxuryEvent: very limited and potentially narrow-hour, market-day, festival, commission, catering, noble/guild-event, or leftover release

liveOwners.observedLimits: no orthogonal food readiness, preparation-method, hazard, portionability, or container-capability profiles

liveOwners.observedAuthority: static consumable energy, protein, carbohydrate, fat, hydration, intoxication, and use verb
liveOwners.observedLimits: no portion basis, satiety, readiness, safety, or meal-composition authority

quantitySystems.recommendation: Treat existing integers as legacy authored recipe units until every affected item declares a compatible basis; do not infer mass, volume, servings, or historical ratios.
quantitySystems.provenanceConfidence: high: directly observed schema and all 28 records
quantitySystems.duplicationOrOwnerConflictRisk: high if culinary code privately assigns units that conflict with workplaces or inventory

quantitySystems.recommendation: Use only the controlled physical dimensions count, mass, and volume. Serving is an authored culinary reference; bundle, batch, contained lot, and package are aggregation or packaging kinds.
quantitySystems.provenanceConfidence: high: cross-domain unit vocabulary measured in live content
quantitySystems.duplicationOrOwnerConflictRisk: medium if the shared type is introduced without content-schema owners

quantitySystems.recommendation: Define stable basis units and separate display units; store amounts as integers or fixed-point basis units. Exact mass and volume bases require explicit acceptance.
quantitySystems.provenanceConfidence: medium: need is clear, exact unit catalog is an open decision
quantitySystems.duplicationOrOwnerConflictRisk: high if workplaces, recipes, and inventory each create their own conversion tables

quantitySystems.recommendation: A serving is an authored culinary reference amount, not a universal physical conversion. It may reference a mass, volume, or discrete-count basis and must not replace the canonical amount.
quantitySystems.provenanceConfidence: high for separation; low for future authored values
quantitySystems.duplicationOrOwnerConflictRisk: medium if nutrition profiles independently define serving sizes

quantitySystems.recommendation: Container templates declare capacity dimension and amount plus allowed fill postures. Instance contents declare current fill; density is optional conversion metadata used only when explicitly authored.
quantitySystems.provenanceConfidence: high: accepted item/inventory boundary; exact fields remain undecided
quantitySystems.duplicationOrOwnerConflictRisk: high if capacity is placed on stacks or parsed from item names

quantitySystems.recommendation: Defer nonculinary migration behind explicit adapters; until then, counts, placeholder yields, and multipliers retain their current domain-local meaning.
quantitySystems.provenanceConfidence: high: direct record and schema audit
quantitySystems.duplicationOrOwnerConflictRisk: medium; compatibility debt is inability to compare yields physically across domains

quantitySystems.recommendation: Retain stack quantity as a presentation/count optimization; divisible or manifested goods require per-instance or per-lot canonical amounts beneath the visible stack.
quantitySystems.provenanceConfidence: high: live stack contract is explicit
quantitySystems.duplicationOrOwnerConflictRisk: high if remaining amount is stored only as an aggregate stack fraction

quantitySystems.recommendation: Market offers must quote item/lot amount and basis without changing static item value identity; bulk containers remain physical inventory instances.
quantitySystems.provenanceConfidence: medium: boundary is clear, transaction command owner is not implemented
quantitySystems.duplicationOrOwnerConflictRisk: high if bulk pricing owns container contents or manifest truth

quantitySystems.recommendation: Starting definitions remain fixed and known; later construction should instantiate accepted quantities, containers, and manifests without randomizing on first open.
quantitySystems.duplicationOrOwnerConflictRisk: medium if UI continues to author instance truth

foodStateConcepts.recommendation: Controlled readiness values distinguish ready_to_eat, requires_preparation, requires_cooking, conditionally_edible, and not_edible_as_presented; readiness is not preservation or safety.
foodStateConcepts.duplicationOrOwnerConflictRisk: high if encoded as a replacement branch taxonomy

foodStateConcepts.recommendation: Use reusable method identities such as bake, boil, dry, ferment, fry, pickle, salt, smoke, steam, and sugar-preserve. Methods may overlap and carry validated effects; recipes/chains reference them.
foodStateConcepts.provenanceConfidence: high for model; exact vocabulary requires review
foodStateConcepts.duplicationOrOwnerConflictRisk: medium if both recipes and production chains claim separate method catalogs

foodStateConcepts.recommendation: Derive or validate preservation posture from controlled methods, parameters, packaging, and resulting profile; do not author a lone isPreserved flag.
foodStateConcepts.provenanceConfidence: high: accepted decision and modern food-safety sources
foodStateConcepts.duplicationOrOwnerConflictRisk: high if preservation is inferred from names or itemSubBranch

foodStateConcepts.recommendation: Orthogonal hazards include biological contamination, parasites, toxin/poisonous part, harmful secretion, spoilage, environmental/chemical contamination, and physical hazards, with residual risk after each supported process.
foodStateConcepts.provenanceConfidence: high for categories; future fantasy biology requires authored input
foodStateConcepts.duplicationOrOwnerConflictRisk: high if generic heat is allowed to clear every hazard

foodStateConcepts.recommendation: Names remain authored. Mechanical fields may validate that an Applewood-Smoked Sausage Links identity references smoking and a fuel/technique descriptor, but mechanics never parse the display name and names are not auto-generated.
foodStateConcepts.duplicationOrOwnerConflictRisk: low when names remain item identity metadata

foodStateConcepts.recommendation: Keep regional, specialty, technique, fuel, quality, elite-display luxury, and attainable-celebratory luxury descriptors separate from readiness and preservation.
foodStateConcepts.provenanceConfidence: medium: semantic direction accepted, lore-native authored content absent
foodStateConcepts.duplicationOrOwnerConflictRisk: medium if descriptors become alternate item identity or price authority

foodStateConcepts.recommendation: Do not repair item.sausage_link, item.sausage_coil, item.smoked_sausage_link, item.skillet_sausage, or sausage-board classifications until the orthogonal food-state contract exists; the current stationery and lighting branches are collisions, while preserved does not prove ready-to-eat.
foodStateConcepts.provenanceConfidence: high: direct item and chain audit
foodStateConcepts.duplicationOrOwnerConflictRisk: high if a taxonomy-only patch lands first

foodStateConcepts.recommendation: Static named recipes may produce durable meal items; ad hoc Ready To Eat and Prepare selections create a deterministic eating occasion or composed-meal instance without inventing a venue-specific recipe identity.
foodStateConcepts.provenanceConfidence: high for boundary; exact persistence choice is open
foodStateConcepts.duplicationOrOwnerConflictRisk: high if UI assembles nutrition totals or mutates inventory

foodStateConcepts.recommendation: Keep serving-basis energy, protein, fat, carbohydrate, hydration, satiety amount/duration, meal aggregation results, exposure/monotony, body-state integration, and difficulty controls in the later consumable-profile v2 and meal/nutrition/difficulty package. Static food-state profiles must not duplicate these fields.
foodStateConcepts.provenanceConfidence: high for existing macros and accepted moderate direction; medium for satiety fields
foodStateConcepts.duplicationOrOwnerConflictRisk: medium if meal preview calculates effects outside player-engine

portionabilitySamples.notes: Cutting does not itself make raw meat safe.
portionabilitySamples.provenanceConfidence: high for separation; exact basis undecided

portionabilitySamples.notes: A required dish/container is selected when physical transfer needs one.
portionabilitySamples.provenanceConfidence: medium: live items exist but no amount/container contract
portionabilitySamples.duplicationOrOwnerConflictRisk: high if bowl identity and food contents are conflated

portionabilitySamples.notes: The current whole-cask consumable profile is not evidence that a cask is one drink.

portionabilitySamples.canonicalAmount: integer count or mass basis chosen per item family
portionabilitySamples.minimumMeaningfulPortion: non-token threshold for nutrition and diversity
portionabilitySamples.notes: Loose carriage normally requires a pouch, basket, sack, or other compatible container.
portionabilitySamples.provenanceConfidence: high for physical intent; exact item profiles require authorship

portionabilitySamples.recommendedMode: whole_only per piece or stack_divisible pieces
portionabilitySamples.notes: A bag may be a container instance; it must not make the entire bag one indivisible food by default.

portionabilitySamples.canonicalAmount: totalAmount and remainingAmount in the same basis
portionabilitySamples.notes: UI percentage sliders convert to deterministic integer amounts; free-floating percentage is never authoritative.
portionabilitySamples.duplicationOrOwnerConflictRisk: high if stored separately by UI and engine

portionabilitySamples.notes: Later freshness and contamination may depend on opening, but this audit does not authorize spoilage runtime.
portionabilitySamples.provenanceConfidence: high for boundary; later behavior deferred
portionabilitySamples.duplicationOrOwnerConflictRisk: high if opening is inferred from remaining amount

containerCapabilityNeeds.recommendation: Declare dimension and maximum basis amount; slot capacity remains a separate bag concept.
Distinguish personal, hand-carried, pack, cart/wagon, and storage postures without making ordinary inventory magical.
Controlled capability forbids liquid transfer into incompatible containers.
Describe food-contact compatibility and later contamination modifiers without claiming modern sanitation knowledge for characters.
containerCapabilityNeeds.provenanceConfidence: high for need; exact mechanics later

containerCapabilityNeeds.recommendation: Declare cold-only, warm-serving, direct-heat, or process-safe posture so Prepare and Cook can validate vessels.
Instance state records open, closed, sealed, locked, and resealed where the template permits; a template describes capability, not current state.
Declare closable, sealable, lockable, and resealable capabilities independently.
Allowed forms include discrete solids, loose solids, powders, pastes, and liquids; lists stay extensible and do not parse tags or names.
Template declares whether nesting is allowed; runtime prevents cycles and enforces capacity.
containerCapabilityNeeds.duplicationOrOwnerConflictRisk: high if bags and item containers create separate nesting graphs

containerCapabilityNeeds.recommendation: Template owns open-view, translucent, opaque, sample-accessible, non-destructively openable, destructively inspectable, sealable, and lockable capabilities. Character observation consumes these capabilities and never owns or gates them.
Engine command validates form, capacity, seal access, and known compatibility; later contamination effects remain a separate risk-resolution package.
containerCapabilityNeeds.provenanceConfidence: high for command ownership; runtime behavior deferred
containerCapabilityNeeds.duplicationOrOwnerConflictRisk: high if UI directly changes contents

knowledgeAndFraudConcepts.recommendation: Resolve true manifest, origin, quality, and relevant condition when the lot or unit is created; opening reveals or samples existing truth and never rerolls contents.
knowledgeAndFraudConcepts.duplicationOrOwnerConflictRisk: high if container opening owns RNG

knowledgeAndFraudConcepts.recommendation: Identical-looking unknown units may share one visible slot while retaining per-unit ids and manifests. Identification or opening splits presentation groups deterministically.
knowledgeAndFraudConcepts.duplicationOrOwnerConflictRisk: high if visible stacking erases per-unit truth

knowledgeAndFraudConcepts.recommendation: Store what this character has observed with certainty/provenance; never copy true identity into a universally visible field by default.
knowledgeAndFraudConcepts.provenanceConfidence: high for separation; exact persistence owner needs acceptance
knowledgeAndFraudConcepts.duplicationOrOwnerConflictRisk: high if Knowledge snippets and item observations both own the same certainty

knowledgeAndFraudConcepts.recommendation: Expose smell, visible condition, season, tradition, trust, preservation practice, and experience rather than pathogens or modern germ theory; hidden engine risk remains authoritative.
knowledgeAndFraudConcepts.provenanceConfidence: high: accepted decision and safety evidence

knowledgeAndFraudConcepts.recommendation: A claim or label is transaction/context state and may disagree with truth; it must not overwrite item identity, origin, manifest, quality, or condition.
knowledgeAndFraudConcepts.provenanceConfidence: high for separation; transaction owner is absent

knowledgeAndFraudConcepts.recommendation: Static methods may describe substitution, short weight, false origin/quality, concealed spoilage, counterfeit mark, mixed lot, or deceptive packing; attempts are context-owned commands.
knowledgeAndFraudConcepts.provenanceConfidence: high for setting concepts; exact skill/ethics owners unresolved
knowledgeAndFraudConcepts.duplicationOrOwnerConflictRisk: high if encoded only as NPC personality text

knowledgeAndFraudConcepts.recommendation: Context selects allowed observations: view sample, inspect deeper, smell, taste, weigh, examine seal/mark/document, or consult. Command accounts for access, permission, deposit, timing, offense, trust, refusal, and destructive opening.
knowledgeAndFraudConcepts.provenanceConfidence: high for action surface; exact resolution contract needs decision
knowledgeAndFraudConcepts.duplicationOrOwnerConflictRisk: high if each vendor UI invents checks

knowledgeAndFraudConcepts.recommendation: Use scoped counterparty/institution evidence and existing local/regional reputation boundaries; do not expose a global omniscient merchant score to new characters.
knowledgeAndFraudConcepts.provenanceConfidence: high for prohibition; exact memory owner unresolved
knowledgeAndFraudConcepts.duplicationOrOwnerConflictRisk: high if player reputation is repurposed as seller truth

knowledgeAndFraudConcepts.recommendation: Difficulty can disable fraud or tune frequency, sophistication, magnitude, inspection forgiveness, and quality/spoilage substitution severity without changing manifest truth.
knowledgeAndFraudConcepts.provenanceConfidence: high for owner boundary; values are balance work

knowledgeAndFraudConcepts.recommendation: Track recent dose by source ingredient/family with dominant share and optional preparation-method facet; exact-item identity alone is exploitable. Decay by elapsed days and allow difficulty reduction or disablement.
knowledgeAndFraudConcepts.provenanceConfidence: high for bounded model; tuning requires tests
knowledgeAndFraudConcepts.duplicationOrOwnerConflictRisk: high if morale, body state, and meal UI each track separate histories

knowledgeAndFraudConcepts.recommendation: Reusable cross-domain profiles own tier, constrained slot pools, weights, floors, quantity ranges, duplicate rules, value bounds, producer/category eligibility, conditions, package reference, and knowledge posture.
knowledgeAndFraudConcepts.provenanceConfidence: high for boundary; exact owner path remains open
knowledgeAndFraudConcepts.duplicationOrOwnerConflictRisk: high if culinary, textile, wood, metal, and apothecary consumers create separate random-box registries

knowledgeAndFraudConcepts.recommendation: Map band_0 through band_3 to category-specific freshness, material, dimensions, process, condition, rarity, and workmanship attributes; bands do not replace physical quality truth.
knowledgeAndFraudConcepts.provenanceConfidence: high for separation; exact mappings remain open
knowledgeAndFraudConcepts.duplicationOrOwnerConflictRisk: high if a universal quality flag erases category truth

knowledgeAndFraudConcepts.recommendation: Own the resolved persisted manifest, condition, price quote, availability window, seller claim, and current stock identity. Resolve at stock generation or immediately pre-transfer, never at opening.
knowledgeAndFraudConcepts.provenanceConfidence: high for truth timing; exact inventory/economy owner remains open
knowledgeAndFraudConcepts.duplicationOrOwnerConflictRisk: high if opening or UI owns manifest generation

knowledgeAndFraudConcepts.currentOwner: descriptive production and economy context only
knowledgeAndFraudConcepts.recommendation: Own finite batch generation, replenishment intervals, withdrawal/expiry, event release, and later demand/sell-through. Static profile authorship does not depend on this schedule.
knowledgeAndFraudConcepts.provenanceConfidence: high for boundary; exact schedule owner remains open
knowledgeAndFraudConcepts.duplicationOrOwnerConflictRisk: high if tier definitions directly simulate stock

knowledgeAndFraudConcepts.recommendation: Track known tier, observed contents, appraisal evidence, and certainty without overwriting the merchant stock manifest.
knowledgeAndFraudConcepts.provenanceConfidence: high for separation; exact persistence owner remains open
knowledgeAndFraudConcepts.duplicationOrOwnerConflictRisk: high if seller claim becomes true contents

knowledgeAndFraudConcepts.recommendation: Purchase, transfer, open, and inspect consume persisted truth and update ownership or observations without rerolling.
knowledgeAndFraudConcepts.provenanceConfidence: high for command boundary; exact engine split remains open
knowledgeAndFraudConcepts.duplicationOrOwnerConflictRisk: high if purchase, inventory, and open each generate different contents

openDecisions.question: Which exact mass and volume basis units, scales, and display conversion rules should the shared quantity contract accept?
Which preparation methods and preservation-effect parameters form the first controlled vocabulary under the accepted future crafting.food_process_methods owner?
Does an ad hoc prepared meal persist as an inventory instance, an immediate eating occasion, or both depending on packaging?
openDecisions.recommendedAnswer: immediate occasion unless deliberately packaged into a compatible container

openDecisions.question: Which hazards can be cleared, reduced, or left residual by each process without implying that heat cures every danger?
Which current food/container records are the minimal representative fixtures for the first schema package?
openDecisions.recommendedAnswer: bread loaf, butchered meat, smoked fish/meat, stew, loose berries/nuts, jar, sack, basket, cask, and glass bottle

openDecisions.question: Should per-item observations be saved as a distinct player collection or evidence records feeding the existing Knowledge framework?
Which existing skills govern appraisal, weighing, seals/documents, smell/taste, and culinary recognition, and is a new domain needed?
What non-token share threshold and decay window should count toward meal diversity and repeated exposure?
Which difficulty tiers disable or soften fraud, monotony, nutrition pressure, and food-risk severity?
What exact ration manifests, physical sizes, kilocalories, serving potential, and balance should each accepted ration name receive?
What exact assortment slot counts, quantity ranges, and later-simulated adjustments, if any, should apply to the candidate tier weights?
What exact reusable static assortment/contextual-quality paths and stock-generation, replenishment, event-release, and demand owners should be accepted?
Which producer/category catalogs, lore-native names, expected-value bounds, and price-variance bounds should later content and balance use?
